rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for trying to see or looking at someone or something.

example.english: Look at what's happening over there.
example.jyutping: nei5 tai2 haa5 go2 bin1 faat3 sang1 me1 si6

rows.note: Use 一眼 for a glance or a brief attempt to see something; it is the all-purpose noun for this sense.

example.english: I want to have a look at the document first.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 jat1 ngaan5 fan6 man4 gin2 sin1

rows.note: Use 樣 for someone’s overall appearance, or colloquially for the facial look they are showing.

example.jyutping: nei5 gam1 jat6 go3 joeng2 hou2 zing1 san4 wo3

rows.note: Use 好似 when “look” means seem or appear to be something.

example.english: You look like you're not feeling well today.
example.jyutping: nei5 gam1 jat6 hou2 ci5 m4 syu1 fuk6 wo3

rows.note: Use 眼神 when the facial expression is conveyed especially through someone’s eyes, such as a dirty or hostile look.

example.english: Their look is really hostile when they stare at me.
example.traditional: 佢望住我嗰陣，眼神好惡。
example.jyutping: keoi5 mong6 zyu6 ngo5 go2 zan6 ngaan5 san4 hou2 ok3

rows.note: Use 表情 for a neutral description of a facial expression, rather than specifically an eye-based look.

example.english: They had a really awkward look after hearing that.
example.traditional: 佢聽到呢句嘢之後，表情好尷尬。
example.jyutping: keoi5 ting1 dou2 ni1 geoi3 je5 zi1 hau6 biu2 cing4 hou2 gaam1 gaai3

rows.note: Use 搵 when looking means searching for or trying to find something.

example.english: I look everywhere but still can't find the book.
example.traditional: 我周圍搵都搵唔到本書。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zau1 wai4 wan2 dou1 wan2 m4 dou2 bun2 syu1

rows.note: Use 睇住 when “look” means to see to something or keep watch to make sure it is handled.

example.english: Can you look after the stove for me?
example.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 zyu6 go3 lou4 fo2
